project.title: What Really Happens When You Use a Cotton Swab?
project.visual_style: cinematic 3D medical anatomy, close macro shots, warm pink ear tissue, visible open ear canal cutaway, realistic soft cotton swab head, amber wax attached to canal wall, dynamic multi-shot camera

narration_beats.text: Your ears make earwax for a reason. It traps dust, tiny particles and helps protect the skin inside your ear canal.
The wax is made in the outer part of the canal. The skin slowly moves outward, carrying old wax toward the ear opening.
Now watch what happens when a cotton swab goes inside. Its soft cotton tip presses against the wax instead of simply lifting it out.
The swab can push that wax farther inward, where it may build up and block the canal. The eardrum sits deeper inside and needs protection.
So don't push cotton swabs into your ear canal. Clean only the outer ear, and get help if you have pain or blocked hearing.
